title: Suitable people and vetting
description: How a nursery checks that the people looking after children are suitable: criminal records checks, references and records. Based on section 3 of the EYFS statutory framework.

lessons.title: Checks before anyone works with children

questions.prompt: A new member of staff can start work while their enhanced criminal records and barred list check is on its way, as long as the manager is happy with them. True or false?

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: False. Providers must not allow individuals to begin working or volunteering at the setting until they have received the applicant’s enhanced criminal records and barred list check. There is an exception for supervised volunteers who only help out occasionally.

learnMore.title: EYFS statutory framework for group and school-based providers

questions.prompt: Who must have an enhanced criminal records check and barred list check?

options.text: Every person aged 16 and over, including volunteers, who works directly with children, or lives or works on the premises where childcare is provided
Only staff who are paid
Only staff who look after children under two
Only the manager

questions.explanation: Registered group and school-based providers must obtain these checks for every person aged 16 and over, including volunteers, who works directly with children, lives on the premises or works on the premises. There are limited exceptions, such as people who do not work where children are cared for, or are not there when children are present.

learnMore.title: EYFS statutory framework for group and school-based providers

questions.prompt: Which of these is correct about references for a new member of staff?

options.text: Get at least one written reference before they are recruited, and do not rely on the applicant to obtain it
A reference “to whom it may concern” is fine
A reference from the applicant’s family member is fine
The applicant can collect their own reference and hand it in

questions.explanation: Providers must obtain at least one written reference for any member of staff, including students and volunteers, before they are recruited. Providers should not accept open references (for example, “to whom it may concern”), should not rely on applicants to obtain their reference, and should not accept references from a family member.

learnMore.title: EYFS statutory framework for group and school-based providers

questions.prompt: What must the provider record about a member of staff’s checks?

options.text: Their qualifications, and the identity checks, vetting processes and references completed, including the criminal records check reference number, the date it was obtained and who at the setting obtained it
Only that they have a DBS certificate somewhere
Only their date of birth
Nothing, as the checks are held by Ofsted

questions.explanation: Providers must record information about staff qualifications and the identity checks, vetting processes and references that have been completed. This includes the criminal records check reference number, the date a check was obtained and details of who at the setting obtained it.

learnMore.title: EYFS statutory framework for group and school-based providers

questions.prompt: Someone who has lived or worked abroad should have an additional criminal records check (or checks, if more than one country). True or false?

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: True. An additional criminal records check (or checks if more than one country) should be made for anyone who has lived or worked abroad.

learnMore.title: EYFS statutory framework for group and school-based providers

questions.prompt: Staff must tell the provider about anything that may affect their suitability to work with children, even if it happens after they have started. True or false?

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: True. Providers must tell staff and prospective staff that they must disclose any information which may affect their suitability, such as arrests, charges, convictions, cautions, court orders, reprimands and warnings, whether received before or during their employment. Convictions or cautions that are protected under the Rehabilitation of Offenders Act 1974 are an exception.

learnMore.title: EYFS statutory framework for group and school-based providers

questions.prompt: When must a provider make a referral to the Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS)?

options.text: When a member of staff is dismissed, or would have been had they not left first, because they have harmed a child or put a child at risk of harm
Whenever a member of staff leaves for any reason
Only when the police ask
Only when a parent complains

questions.explanation: Providers are required to make a referral to the DBS if a member of staff is dismissed (or would have been, had they not left the setting first) because they have harmed a child or put a child at risk of harm.

questions.prompt: Sam is a new member of staff. Their enhanced criminal records and barred list check has not come back yet. The room is short-staffed and Sam offers to take two children to the garden on their own.

choices.text: Say no. Until the check has been received and looked at, Sam cannot have unsupervised contact with children, and they should not start work yet
choices.feedback: Right. Providers must not allow anyone whose suitability has not been checked to have unsupervised contact with children.

choices.text: Say yes, because Sam seems capable
choices.feedback: Not checked means no unsupervised contact with children, however capable someone seems.

choices.text: Say yes, but only for ten minutes
choices.feedback: There is no short-time exception. Unchecked people must not have unsupervised contact with children.

questions.explanation: Providers must not allow individuals to begin working at the setting until they have received the applicant’s enhanced criminal records and barred list check, and must not allow anyone whose suitability has not been checked to have unsupervised contact with children.
